recall_prompt: Say how you would find 13 C n when n C 5 equals n C 6.
insider_note: State the identity line before using it: unequal lower numbers mean n = 5 + 6 = 11. Then finish what was asked — ¹³C₁₁ = ¹³C₂ = 78 — because n itself is not the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Use ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₛ ⇒ r = s or r + s = n
steps.margin_note: First mark. State the identity. 5 ≠ 6, so the second case applies: n = 5 + 6 = 11.
steps.memory_tip: 5 ≠ 6, so n = 5 + 6 = 11. State the identity before using it.
lines: ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₛ ⇒ r = s or r + s = n

recall.must_convey: That n C r equals n C s means r equals s or r plus s equals n, and since 5 is not 6, n = 11.
accept: n C r equals n C s means r is s or r plus s is n, five is not six so n is five plus six eleven
the two lower numbers add to n so n is eleven
n is five plus six which is eleven
n C r equal n C s ante r plus s equal n, so n eleven
use the rule that the lower numbers add up to n

steps.why: ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ because choosing r things is the same as leaving out n − r. So two different lower numbers give the same value only when they add to n.
common_mistakes: Writing n = 5 + 6 without stating the identity that allows it.
Trying to solve ⁿC₅ = ⁿC₆ by expanding both — it works but takes far longer than two marks allow.

steps.label: Evaluate ¹³C₁₁
steps.memory_tip: Finish what was asked: ¹³C₁₁ = ¹³C₂ = (13 × 12)/2 = 78. n alone is not the answer.

recall.must_convey: That 13 C 11 is 13 C 2, which is 13 times 12 over 2 = 78.
accept: thirteen C eleven is thirteen C two which is thirteen into twelve by two equals seventy eight
thirteen C eleven equals thirteen C two equals seventy eight
thirteen C eleven ni thirteen C two ga rasi seventy eight

steps.why: The same identity ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ turns ¹³C₁₁ into ¹³C₂, two factors instead of eleven. The answer is a number, not a symbol.
common_mistakes: Computing 13 · 12 = 156 and forgetting to divide by 2.
